GPT-6.2 Astra (Max) by @OpenAI ranks #6 on the Agent Arena Index, one place above GPT-6 Astra (Max). 
However, these models excel in very different capabilities. Let’s dive in by index.

GPT-6.2 Astra vs GPT-6 Astra across key Agent Arena Indexes:
- Coding: 1,338 vs 1,288 (+50)
- Work: 1,280 vs 1,267 (+13)
- Chat: 1,211 vs 1,265 (-54)

This shows the new model’s gain is in coding, where GPT-6.2 Astra climbs from #8 to #3. On Chat, the everyday tasks such as research, tutoring or writing, it drops from #8 to #11. The two shifts nearly cancel out in the overall score.

I asked GLM 5.4 for a detailed Grim Reaper voxel scene, it came back with moonlight, long shadows, a full animation rig and a soundtrack on its own, on top of it!

It reviewed its own work with headless-Chrome screenshots and caught and corrected bugs on its own really well. Nobody told it to do that either.

Then I asked for sound. It synthesized an entire soundtrack with the Web Audio API: gusting wind, a D-minor drone, crickets, an owl, a raven, a church bell, a music-box motif, all through a reverb it generated from decaying noise!!! Again on its own. Footsteps are panned to where the beast actually is relative to your camera as it circles the yard. 🤯

To be clear, much of what I said has been said by the leaders of other labs. What I *am* saying is this path is not inevitable.

I am saying leaders and leadership matter more than ever, and that’s why I’m proud of the work that Mark and I have done at Meta to put safety as a top focus of our efforts, including delaying the launch of Muse for months and being a leader on the SI Accords that all of our peers have signed onto. We are investing more in safety every day, and have implemented rigorous processes to make sure every step we take is safe and positive. Mark has also called for all labs (including our own) to deploy the vast majority of compute towards serving people and customers rather than towards recursive self-improvement (RSI).
